'''Michael James Duff''' [[Royal Society|FRS]] is a British theoretical physicist known for his contributions to quantum gravity, Kaluza-Klein theory, supergravity, string theory and M-theory. He is Emeritus Professor and Distinguished Research Fellow in the Physics Department, Imperial College London.

==Education==
Duff attended De La Salle College in Salford,1960-1966. He received his BSc in Physics from [[Queen Mary, University of London|Queen Mary College, London]] in 1969 and Diploma of Imperial College and PhD in Theoretical  Physics from [[Imperial College London]] in 1972. His supervisor was [[Nobel Laureate]] [[Abdus Salam]].

==Academic career==
He undertook postdoctoral fellowships at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]], [[University of Oxford]], [[King's College London]], [[Queen Mary, University of London|Queen Mary College London]] and [[Brandeis University]]. He returned to Imperial College as a member of staff in 1979, taking leave of absence to visit the Theory Division at [[CERN]], first in 1982 and then again as a Staff Member from 1984 to 1987 when he became Senior Physicist. He took up his professorship at [[Texas A&M University]] in 1988 and was appointed Distinguished Professor in 1992. In 1999 he became Oskar Klein Professor of Physics at the [[University of Michigan]] and was elected to serve as first Director of the Michigan Center for Theoretical Physics 2000-2005. In 2005 he returned once more to Imperial where he has served as Principal of the Faculty of Physical Sciences and Abdus Salam Professor of Theoretical Physics. He was Leverhulme Fellow and Visiting Professor of Mathematics at Oxford 2017-2020. He is now Emeritus Professor of Theoretical Physics and Distinguished Research Fellow at Imperial.

==Research==
Duff's interests lie in unified theories of the [[elementary particles]], [[quantum gravity]], [[supergravity]], [[Kaluza–Klein theory]], [[superstrings]], [[branes|supermembranes]], [[M-theory]] and [[Quantum information|quantum information theory.]] Notable achievements include:

* Quantum corrections to the Schwarzschild solution.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duff |first=M. J. |date=1974-03-15 |title=Quantum corrections to the Schwarzschild solution |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.9.1837 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=9 |issue=6 |pages=1837–1839 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.9.1837 |bibcode=1974PhRvD...9.1837D |issn=0556-2821|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 
* The discovery of Weyl anomalies: the invariance under local rescalings of the metric tensor of classical massless fields coupled to gravity no longer survives in the quantum theory.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duff |first=M.J. |date=July 1977 |title=Observations on conformal anomalies |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321377904102 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=125 |issue=2 |pages=334–348 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(77)90410-2 |bibcode=1977NuPhB.125..334D |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Spin 3/2 chiral anomaly.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Christensen |first1=S.M. |last2=Duff |first2=M.J. |date=July 1978 |title=Axial and conformal anomalies for arbitrary spin in gravity and supergravity |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269378908572 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=76 |issue=5 |pages=571–574 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(78)90857-2 |bibcode=1978PhLB...76..571C |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 3-form origin of the cosmological constant.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duff |first1=M.J. |last2=van Nieuwenhuizen |first2=P. |date=July 1980 |title=Quantum inequivalence of different field representations |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269380908527 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=94 |issue=2 |pages=179–182 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(80)90852-7 |bibcode=1980PhLB...94..179D |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Kaluza-Klein supergravity, in particular the compactification of D=11 Supergravity on the round and squashed seven-sphere, and on K3.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duff |first1=M |last2=Nilsson |first2=Bengt E.W. |last3=Pope |first3=Christopher N. |date=January 1986 |title=Kaluza-Klein supergravity |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370157386901638 |journal=Physics Reports |volume=130 |issue=1–2 |pages=1–142 |doi=10.1016/0370-1573(86)90163-8 |bibcode=1986PhR...130....1D |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* The connection between holonomy and supersymmetry.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Awada |first1=M. A. |last2=Duff |first2=M. J. |last3=Pope |first3=C. N. |date=1983-01-31 |title=N = 8 Supergravity Breaks Down to N = 1 |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.294 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=50 |issue=5 |pages=294–297 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.294 |bibcode=1983PhRvL..50..294A |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Pioneering work on "branes"<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duff |first=M J |date=1988-01-01 |title=Supermembranes: the first fifteen weeks |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0264-9381/5/1/023 |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=189–205 |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/5/1/023 |bibcode=1988CQGra...5..189D |issn=0264-9381}}</ref>, which initially met with fierce resistance from the string community until vindicated by M-Theory.<ref>{{cite book|editor-first=M. J. |editor-last= Duff|title=The World in Eleven Dimensions: Supergravity, Supermembranes and M-theory|isbn=978-0-7503-0672-0|year= 1999|publisher= Taylor & Francis}}</ref>  In particular:  branes as soliton solutions of string theory<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duff |first1=M |date=August 1995 |title=String solitons |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/037015739500002X |journal=Physics Reports |language=en |volume=259 |issue=4–5 |pages=213–326 |doi=10.1016/0370-1573(95)00002-X|last2=Khuri|first2=Ramzi R.|last3=Lu|first3=J. X. |arxiv=hep-th/9412184 |bibcode=1995PhR...259..213D }}</ref>; the S-duality of the fundamental string as T-duality of the dual solitonic string.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duff |first=M. J. |date=1995-05-22 |title=Strong/weak coupling duality from the dual string |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0550321395000704 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=442 |issue=1 |pages=47–63 |doi=10.1016/S0550-3213(95)00070-4 |arxiv=hep-th/9501030 |bibcode=1995NuPhB.442...47D |issn=0550-3213}}</ref> The Oxford English Dictionary attributes first usage of the word "brane" to Duff’s 1987 paper with Inami, Pope, Sezgin and Stelle.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duff |first1=M.J. |last2=Inami |first2=T. |last3=Pope |first3=C.N. |last4=Sezgin |first4=E. |last5=Stelle |first5=K.S. |date=February 1988 |title=Semiclassical quantization of the supermembrane |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321388903161 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=297 |issue=3 |pages=515–538 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(88)90316-1 |bibcode=1988NuPhB.297..515D |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Contributions to M-theory; superstrings in D=10 from supermembranes in D=11<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duff |first1=M.J. |last2=Howe |first2=P.S. |last3=Inami |first3=T. |last4=Stelle |first4=K.S. |date=June 1987 |title=Superstrings in D=10 from supermembranes in D=11 |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269387913232 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=191 |issue=1–2 |pages=70–74 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(87)91323-2 |bibcode=1987PhLB..191...70D |url-access=subscription }}</ref>; M2 solutions of D=11 supergravity<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duff |first1=M.J. |last2=Stelle |first2=K.S. |date=January 1991 |title=Multi-membrane solutions of D = 11 supergravity |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269391913712 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=253 |issue=1–2 |pages=113–118 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(91)91371-2 |bibcode=1991PhLB..253..113D |url-access=subscription }}</ref>; the M5-brane anomaly<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Duff |first1=M.J. |last2=Liu |first2=James T. |last3=Minasian |first3=R. |date=October 1995 |title=Eleven-dimensional origin of string/string duality: a one-loop test |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321395003683 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=452 |issue=1–2 |pages=261–282 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(95)00368-3 |arxiv=hep-th/9506126 |bibcode=1995NuPhB.452..261D }}</ref>; evidence for Heterotic/Heterotic duality<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duff |first1=M.J. |last2=Minasian |first2=R. |last3=Witten |first3=Edward |date=April 1996 |title=Evidence for heterotic/heterotic duality |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321396000594 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=465 |issue=3 |pages=413–438 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(96)00059-4 |arxiv=hep-th/9601036 |bibcode=1996NuPhB.465..413D }}</ref>.
* Double geometry<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duff |first=M.J. |date=May 1990 |title=Duality rotations in string theory |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/055032139090520N |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=335 |issue=3 |pages=610–620 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(90)90520-N |bibcode=1990NuPhB.335..610D |url-access=subscription }}</ref>: T-duality made manifest by considering a target space of double the dimension with coordinates ''Z<sup>M</sup>'' = (''x<sup>μ</sup>'', ''y<sub>α</sub>'').

== Other Publications ==
He is the editor of "The World in Eleven Dimensions: Supergravity, Supermembranes and M-theory"<ref name=":2" />, a collection of notable scientific articles on eleven dimensions; "Stephen Weinberg: Collected Papers’"<ref>{{Cite book |title=Steven Weinberg: selected papers |date=2023 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-12-6135-0 |editor-last=Weinberg |editor-first=Steven |location=New Jersey |editor-last2=Duff |editor-first2=Michael James}}</ref>; "Memorial Volume on Abdus Salam's 90th Birthday"<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Brink |first1=Lars |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/10161 |title=Memorial Volume on Abdus Salam's 90th Birthday |last2=Duff |first2=Michael |last3=Phua |first3=Kok Khoo |date=May 2017 |publisher=WORLD SCIENTIFIC |isbn=978-981-314-486-6 |language=en |doi=10.1142/10161 |bibcode=2017mvas.book.....B }}</ref> and "Salam +50"<ref>{{Cite book |title=Salam + 50: proceedings of the conference |date=2008 |publisher=Imperial College Press ; Distributed by World Scientific |isbn=978-1-84816-190-0 |editor-last=Duff |editor-first=M. J. |location=London : Singapore ; Hackensack, N.J}}</ref>.

== Honors and Awards ==
He is a Fellow of the Royal Society<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |title=Professor Michael Duff FRS {{!}} Royal Society Fellow |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/michael-duff-11362/ |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=royalsociety.org |language=en}}</ref>, a Fellow of the American Physical Society<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Duff {{!}} About {{!}} Imperial College London |url=https://profiles.imperial.ac.uk/m.duff |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=profiles.imperial.ac.uk}}</ref>, a Fellow of the Institute of Physics, a Member of the London Mathematical Society, Recipient of the 2004 Meeting Gold Medal, El Colegio Nacional, Mexico; the 2017 Paul Dirac Gold Medal and Prize, Institute of Physics, UK;  the 2018 Trotter Prize, USA. He was inducted as 2019 Faculty Fellow of the Hagler Institute for Advanced Study, Texas A&M University.  A special issue of Proceedings of the Royal Society was dedicated to Michael on the occasion of his 70th birthday "[https://royalsocietypublishing.org/rspa/collection/59/Quantum-gravity-branes-and-M-theory Quantum Gravity, Branes and M-theory]",  L. Borsten, A. Marrani,  C.N Pope and  K.Stelle  (Editors)

His nomination for the Royal Society reads<ref name="Website-1" />:<blockquote>Michael Duff is a theoretical physicist who has made significant contributions to the unification of quantum mechanics and Albert Einstein’s theory of general relativity. His work has been instrumental in the development of quantum gravity, supergravity, string theory and M-theory. He was instrumental in the discovery of conformal anomalies and the applications of index theorems in supergravity. He is also known for his early work on Kaluza–Klein theory, a unified field theory of gravitation and the other forces in higher spacetime dimensions. Michael also wrote the first book devoted to M-theory, The World in Eleven Dimensions: Supergravity, Supermembranes and M-theory, which he published in 1999. His scientific ideas have been published in newspapers and magazines such as The Independent, The Guardian and New Scientist.</blockquote>

== Personal Life ==
Duff was born in Manchester, younger brother of Anne and John. He married Lesley (nee Yearling) in 1984. They have two children; Jessica born 1986 and Matthew born 1988.
